name: Cisco FMC
description: Cisco Firepower Management Center. Deployment health, disk, database, backup, licensing, and expert-mode diagnostics.
notes: Most FMC workflows start in the web UI; the CLI is intentionally limited.
Expert mode is a Linux shell. Use read-only commands.
FMC does not manage traffic inline; FTD is the enforcement point.

categories.name: System health
categories.description: CPU, memory, disk, database, and health monitor.

categories.name: Expert mode
categories.description: Linux-level checks for disk, services, and logs.

workflows.title: FMC health snapshot
workflows.summary: Collect version, CPU, memory, disk, and process state from the CLI and health monitor.

steps.instruction: In the FMC UI, open System > Health > Monitor and check the health policy for the management center.

notes: A high CPU reading during a deploy or report can be normal. Compare against the health monitor history.

workflows.title: Disk full or database pressure
workflows.summary: Check disk usage, large files, and the health alerts that indicate database or disk pressure.

steps.instruction: In the FMC UI, open System > Health > Monitor and review disk and database alerts.
In expert mode, run 'sudo df -h' and check the partitions that are above 85 percent.
Review System > Tools > Backup and remove old backups only after confirming a current backup exists.

notes: Never delete database files directly. Use the FMC UI and Cisco support guidance.

workflows.title: Device deployment failures
workflows.summary: Trace a failed FTD deployment through device status, tasks, and policy validation.

steps.instruction: Open Devices > Device Management and check the FTD status, registration, and last deploy time.
Open Tasks and read the failed deploy task. Expand policy validation and device communication errors.
Check the FTD side with 'show managers' to confirm it is still registered to this FMC.
If the failure is policy-related, inspect the access control, NAT, and platform settings that changed.

notes: A device that shows as unreachable needs network and sftunnel checks before policy troubleshooting.

workflows.title: FTD registration and sftunnel
workflows.summary: Confirm the FMC-to-FTD management tunnel and registration state.

steps.instruction: In FMC, open Devices > Device Management and check the device status and last seen time.
On the FTD CLI, run 'show managers' and confirm the FMC address and registration state.
If the tunnel is down, verify management IP, default route, DNS, and TCP 8305 between FTD and FMC.
After connectivity is restored, refresh the device in FMC and retry the deployment.

workflows.title: Expert mode — services and logs
workflows.summary: Use read-only Linux commands to inspect disk, memory, services, and recent logs.

steps.instruction: From the FMC CLI, run 'expert' and enter the expert password.
Exit expert mode when finished. Do not restart services without Cisco guidance.

notes: Expert mode is a root Linux shell. Use it for observation, not for changes during an incident.

workflows.title: Backup and restore readiness
workflows.summary: Verify that a recent configuration backup exists and that the restore target is compatible.

steps.instruction: Open System > Tools > Backup/Restore and check the latest backup status and timestamp.
Confirm the backup is stored off the FMC appliance.
Record the FMC version and build; a restore target must run the same or a supported version.
Check that the backup includes the configuration and, if required, the events data.

workflows.title: Smart licensing status
workflows.summary: Inspect registration, entitlements, and expired or out-of-compliance licenses.

steps.instruction: Open System > Licenses > Smart Licenses and check the registration status.
Review the entitlement table for expired, out-of-compliance, or insufficient licenses.
Check the FTD device licenses under Devices > Device Management > Licenses.
If registration is stale, verify outbound HTTPS to the Cisco licensing service.

workflows.title: Security intelligence updates
workflows.summary: Check URL, DNS, and intelligence feed update status.

steps.instruction: Open System > Updates and review the last update times for intelligence feeds.
Check Tasks for failed update jobs and the reported error.
Verify the FMC can reach the Cisco update service over HTTPS.
Compare the feed version with the FTDs to confirm the devices have received the update.

workflows.title: Time and NTP
workflows.summary: Verify the FMC clock and NTP synchronization because auth and correlation depend on it.

steps.instruction: In the FMC UI, open System > Configuration > Time and confirm the NTP servers.
